questions.prompt: Cicero was a famous orator, whom everyone used to admire.
questions.answer: Cicerō ōrātor clārus fuit, quem omnēs admīrābantur.

questions.prompt: Numa, after Romulus had died, was elected king by the Romans.
questions.answer: Numa, Rōmulō mortuō, rēx ā Rōmānīs creātus est.

questions.prompt: Philosophy, which teaches wisdom, is the guide of life.
questions.answer: Philosophia, quae sapientiam docet, magistra vītae est.

questions.prompt: Romulus, when he had founded the city, was called king.
questions.answer: Rōmulus, cum urbem condidisset, rēx appellātus est.

questions.prompt: Because he despised the gods, he was regarded as an impious man.
questions.answer: Quia deōs contempsit, homō impius habitus est.

questions.prompt: The proconsul, ambitious and cruel, seemed a tyrant to the provincials.
questions.answer: Prōcōnsul, ambitiōsus et crūdēlis, prōvinciālibus tyrannus vidēbātur.

questions.prompt: The consuls were made leaders of the state by the people's vote.
questions.answer: Cōnsulēs suffrāgiō populī reī pūblicae ducēs factī sunt.

questions.prompt: Although he was born a poor man, he died a rich one.
questions.answer: Quamquam pauper nātus est, dīves mortuus est.

questions.prompt: Caesar, after the Gauls had been conquered, was regarded as a god by many.
questions.answer: Caesar, Gallīs victīs, ā multīs deus habēbātur.

questions.prompt: By this victory you will be made the glory of your people.
questions.answer: Hāc victōriā populī tuī glōria fīēs.

questions.prompt: Numa, although a foreigner, was elected king by the Romans.
questions.answer: Numa, quamquam peregrīnus, ā Rōmānīs rēx creātus est.

questions.prompt: The old man, once a soldier, remained the faithful guardian of the temple.
questions.answer: Senex, ōlim mīles, fīdus templī custōs mānsit.

questions.prompt: Cicero, whom the citizens admired, was regarded as the father of his country.
questions.answer: Cicerō, quem cīvēs mīrābantur, pater patriae habitus est.

questions.prompt: The young man, rude and untrained, turned out to be a most skilled farmer.
questions.answer: Adulēscēns, rudis et indoctus, agricola perītissimus ēvāsit.

questions.prompt: Wealth does not make bad men good citizens.
questions.answer: Dīvitiae malōs virōs bonōs cīvēs nōn faciunt.

questions.prompt: From a humble slave he emerged as leader of the army.
questions.answer: Ex humilī servō dux exercitūs exstitit.

questions.prompt: Caesar, once the Rubicon had been crossed, seemed a tyrant to many.
questions.answer: Caesar, Rubicōne trānsitō, multīs tyrannus vidēbātur.

questions.prompt: After the long war had ended, the exhausted soldier became a farmer.
questions.answer: Bellō longō cōnfectō, mīles fessus agricola factus est.

questions.prompt: Although he was born a slave, he turned out to be a most faithful friend.
questions.answer: Quamquam servus nātus erat, amīcus fīdēlissimus ēvāsit.

questions.prompt: Philosophy, which we cultivate with great zeal, is the guide of life.
questions.answer: Philosophia, quam magnō studiō colimus, vītae magistra est.

questions.prompt: Having conquered the enemy, the general was regarded by all as a god.
questions.answer: Hostibus victīs, dux ab omnibus deus habitus est.

questions.prompt: The boy, once frightened by the storm, was afterward called a brave sailor.
questions.answer: Puer, turbine ōlim territus, posteā nauta fortis appellātus est.

questions.prompt: After the king had been driven out, the two consuls were created leaders of the state.
questions.answer: Rēge expulsō, duo cōnsulēs cīvitātis prīncipēs creātī sunt.

questions.prompt: That woman, whom we all praise, seems to be the truest guardian of the temple.
questions.answer: Illa mulier, quam omnēs laudāmus, vērissima templī custōs vidētur.

questions.prompt: For what is an exile?
questions.answer: Quid est enim exsul?

questions.prompt: For the glory of riches and beauty is fleeting and fragile, but virtue is held to be glorious and everlasting.
questions.answer: Nam dīvitiārum et fōrmae glōria flū̆xa atque fragilis est, virtūs clāra aeternaque habētur.

questions.prompt: All Gaul is divided into three parts, of which the Belgae inhabit one, the Aquitani another, and the third those who in their own language are called Celts, in ours Gauls.
questions.answer: Gallia est omnis dīvīsa in partēs trēs, quārum ūnam incolunt Belgae, aliam Aquītānī, tertiam quī ipsōrum linguā Celtae, nostrā Gallī appellantur.

questions.prompt: Marcus Varro defines it thus: 'A line,' he says, 'is a certain length without breadth and height.'.
questions.answer: Eam [līneam] M. [Mārcus] Varrō ita dēfīnit: "Līnea est," inquit, "longitūdō quaedam sine lātitūdine et altitūdine."

questions.prompt: From his country house both Curius and the other old men used to be summoned into the Senate; from which those who summoned them were called viatores.
questions.answer: Ā vīllā in Senātum arcessēbātur et Curius et cēterī senēs; ex quō, quī eōs arcessēbant viātōrēs nōminātī sunt.

questions.prompt: Pen is the best professor of rhetoric.
questions.answer: stilus optimus dīcendī magister.

questions.prompt: Country life is a teacher of thrift.
questions.answer: vīta rūstica parsimōniae magistra est.

questions.prompt: To say nothing of the great originator of all intellectual pursuits, Athens.
questions.answer: ut omittam illās omnium doctrīnārum inventrīcēs Athēnās.
